sentence: A repository, and each member of a workspace, declares what it is once — its kind and its platform — in jterrazz.config.ts.
A settings file loads synchronously too, since the oxlint rules read jterrazz.config.ts so, and one they cannot load would leave them judging on defaults.
Each config file an editor discovers is the file jterrazz.config.ts derives, so the editor and the check judge alike.

An editor file sits in the unit it is derived for: the oxlint and oxfmt configs at the repository root alone, a tsconfig.json — or a preset's file such as vitest.config.ts — in each declared project, and never at a workspace root, which declares no platform.
A tool only the toolchain runs keeps no config file of its own: the command hands it the config jterrazz.config.ts derives.
A library publishes its exports, a published cli names its bin, and an application — an api, a website, a mobile app — is private, never published, as is a workspace's own suite.

A project is an ES module, its manifest setting "type": "module": the vitest config the toolchain derives and the names its build gives the files are ESM's, and a package without it fails in both without saying why.
A manifest holds the top-level keys npm and the family's tools read: a key beyond them reads nothing, and a typo of one fails without a word.
What typescript.tsconfig adds to the derived tsconfig.json carries its reason, since every setting maps to why it is set.
A package's standard under src/standard/ is data: no function, branch, call or variable but the defineStandard each file exports.
A comment run above a function is no longer than the function it documents.

A comment opens with the kind of thing it states — invariant, hazard, outside or value — unless it is an exported symbol's hover doc (one line of prose, its block tags after it), a directive or a marker another tool reads, whose reason states none.
A `*.data.ts` module holds its imports, its types and the literals it exports — no function, class or statement — so the file-size cap stands aside for its rows.
An `errors.ts` or `*.errors.ts` module holds one family of classes — a base and what derives from it — so the class-count cap stands aside for it.
An element whose role, tab stop or aria attribute is set is written in JSX, never through `createElement`, whose props no jsx-a11y rule reads.
A `<section>` that takes the keyboard's focus names the region it scrolls with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, since an unlabelled section is no region and its `tabIndex` a stray tab stop.

A promise is awaited, never threaded through a `.then()`, `.catch()` or `.finally()` chain nor wrapped in an async function called at the module's top level — and a `.catch()` given a value, which no promise takes, is a schema's fallback the rule leaves alone.
`matchAll` is not given a pattern with a named group on Hermes, whose iterator leaves `match.groups` undefined.
A comment of a style sheet, a shell script, a Makefile, a Dockerfile or a YAML file opens with its kind, as a comment of code does — unless it is a directive another tool reads.
A suppression is spelled for the linter this toolchain runs: oxlint-disable, never eslint-disable or biome-ignore.
Every oxlint-disable and Stryker disable directive states the reason it exists.
A Stryker disable directive names the mutators it declares equivalent, never all of them.
A Stryker next-line directive stands where a mutant starts on the next line: never above a line led by a closing brace, never in a JSX comment container.
A directory or file is named for the subject it holds, never a grab-bag word.
A directory or file is named for its subject, never for a construct of the language.
Every word of a name is spelled whole.
A directory under a named root is written in kebab-case, a route segment in its framework's grammar.
Every root folder is on the root spine, imposed by a tool, or declared with its reason.
A root declared in typescript.roots states why the repository keeps it.
A root declared in typescript.roots is a first-level folder that is no folder of the spine.
A root declared in typescript.roots holds a file git does not ignore.
The settings file jterrazz.config.ts loads, and its typescript section has the declared shape.
A skill is one skills/<skill>/SKILL.md and the references/*.md pages it links, and nothing else beside it.
Every repository root carries a Makefile.
The Makefile writes a rule for each of the six gestures.
No directory of the working copy is empty.
why: git tracks no directory, so an empty one exists only on this machine and names a part of the tree that is not there

sentence: The source a published subpath is built from is named index[.<subpath>][.browser].ts, and a bin's <command>.bin.ts.
A module named <command>.bin is the entry of a bin the package publishes under that command, or that entry's test.
A module named index is the entry of a subpath the package publishes or of a private import it declares, or that entry's test.
Every subpath and bin the package publishes as code is compiled by its build, from a source the build names.
Every backticked repository path of a page names something on disk or in a tree git ignores, but in a decision record, which names the paths of its day.
Every relative link of a page reaches a file on disk or a tree git ignores.
A skill's SKILL.md links every page of its references/ folder, since a reference nothing points to is one no agent opens.
Every page a skill names is one its package ships.
A paragraph or a list item runs twelve lines at most.
A fenced block breathes within fifteen lines.
A section over thirty prose lines is broken by a subheading or a list.
No committed file carries a private key block.
No committed file carries an aws access key.
No committed file carries a github token.
No committed file carries a slack token.
No committed file carries a tailscale key.
No committed file carries a signed jwt.
No committed file carries a grafana token.
No committed file carries an api key.
No committed file carries a bank account number.
No committed file carries a service token.
Every repository carries a docs/ manual.
The root AGENTS.md routes to the manual's map.
The manual opens on its map, docs/README.md.
The map links every page of the four sections, and only the pages there are.
The map links nothing but its own pages and decisions/.
A page is named kebab-case.md, with no number.
A section holds pages and no folder.
The manual holds concepts/architecture.md, guides/develop.md and guides/test.md.
A repository that ships an image or a package carries guides/release.md.
A page is named for a subject, never for the state of a piece of work.
The only file directly under docs/ is the map.
The manual holds no folder but start/, guides/, concepts/, reference/, decisions/ and _assets/.
No link of the manual reaches into another repository's tree.
A decision record is named NNN-kebab.md.
A decision record opens on # ADR-NNN: Title, with its own number.
One ADR number belongs to one record.
Decision records are numbered from 001 without a gap.
A decision record states a status from the closed vocabulary.
The decisions folder keeps no hand-written index, no decisions/README.md: the map links the folder, and the records list themselves.
A manual that keeps a decisions folder carries its _template.md in it.
Every target the exports, main and types fields name exists on disk.
Every target the exports, main and types fields name is published by files.
The build the guard reads succeeds.
No shipped file is compiled from test material.
The root of lint/ holds its entries alone, each index[.<name>].ts built as a published subpath or a private import.
Every folder of lint/ is one of consumer, self and kit.
Every folder of lint/consumer/ is one of catalogue, rulebook, rules and checks, and no file sits at its root.
Every folder of lint/self/ is one of catalogue, rules, checks and corpus, and only the modules composing them sit at its root.
Every folder of lint/kit/ is one of project, baseline, checker, catalogue, compiler and testing, and no file sits at its root.
A module under lint/consumer/ or lint/self/ is a declaration: it runs as no program, and hands another module no function but one named for its file.
A rule file sits under rules/<family>/, the family its catalogue row declares.
